raw_text: Natural Products
Total Synthesis of (+)-Kalmanol
Tianhao Ma, Yiming Ma, Bo Li, and Yanxing Jia\*

Abstract: Kalmanol, the flagship member of the kalmane diterpene family, possesses a complex and highly oxidized 5/5/8/5 tetracyclic skeleton with nine contiguous stereocenters and exhibits significant analgesic effects and cardiotoxic properties. We have achieved the efficient total synthesis of (+)-kalmanol in 22 steps with 2.3% yield. The synthesis featured a Rh-catalyzed [5+2 +1] cycloaddition reaction to construct 5/5/8 tricyclic skeleton, and a meticulously designed sequence of stereoselective oxidations of the 5/5/8/5 tetracyclic skeleton.

Kalmane diterpenoids possess a unique 5/5/8/5 tetracyclic skeleton and are exclusively present in Ericaceae plants (Figure 1). Since the first compound kalmanol (1) was isolated by Clardy and co-workers from the Kalmia angustifolia L. in 1989,<sup>[1]</sup> only less than 20 kalmane diterpenoids have been isolated and identified to date.<sup>[2]</sup> In contrast, more than 300 grayanane diterpenoids have been isolated and identified to date and they are also exclusively present in Ericaceae plants,<sup>[3]</sup> and many elegant total syntheses had been accomplished.<sup>[4–8]</sup> Biosynthetically, the 1,2- rearrangement of C8�C9 bond to C14 from the grayanotoxin III (2) can provide the kalmane 5/8/5/5 tetracyclic skeleton.<sup>[1]</sup> The preliminary bioactivity studies showed that kalmanol (1) exhibited more potent analgesic activities than morphine even at lower doses of 0.2 and 0.04 mg/kg with inhibition rates of 63.7 % (0.2 mg/kg) and 54.7 % (0.04 mg/kg), respectively.<sup>[2]</sup> Meanwhile, kalmanol exhibited cardiotoxic properties which produced a 23% increase in systolictension at $\bar { 1 } . 7 { \times } 1 0 ^ { - 5 } \mathrm { { M } }$ of concentration and higher concentrations induced arrhythmia.<sup>[1]</sup> However, the scarce availability from natural sources $( 1 . 2 { \times } 1 0 ^ { - 3 } \%$ of dry weight) has restricted the further medicinal evaluation of kalmanol, “A fuller evalua tion must await procurement of more material" [1]

The unique 5/5/8/5 tetracyclic skeleton and important biological activities had made them attractive targets for total synthesis.<sup>[9–12]</sup> In 1995 and 1996, Paquette’s group have reported the synthetic studies toward kalmanol, and achieved the synthesis of the targeted tetracyclic framework by 3,3-Claisen rearrangement ring expansion.<sup>[9]</sup> In 2023, the group of Luo disclosed the first total synthesis of (+)-kalma nol in 22 LLS (longest linear sequence) with 0.06 % overall yield.<sup>[10]</sup> Recently, our group also reported the total synthesis of (+)-kalmanol in 29 LLS with 0.16 % overall yield.<sup>[11]</sup> Very recently, the group of Ding reported the ring-distortion approach for the synthesis of kalmane 5/8/5/5 skeleton.<sup>[12]</sup> Indeed, both Luo’s and our group employed the biomimetic 1,2-rearrangement of grayanane 5/7/6/5 skeleton to generate kalmane 5/8/5/5 skeleton. Although these two syntheses are elegant approaches, they are not practical and cannot solve the supply problem of kalmanol. Therefore, the development of approaches that would allow the facile preparation of large amount of kalmanol and its derivatives were still highly desirable.

raw_text: In recent years, several transition-metal-catalyzed cycloadditions,<sup>[13]</sup> especially Rh-catalyzed [5+2+1] cycloaddition,<sup>[14,15]</sup> have been proved to be one of elegant approaches for the one-step construction of 5/8-fused ring systems, and this method was successfully applied to the total synthesis of natural products.<sup>[16]</sup> However, this [5 + 2 + 1] reaction has not yet been used in constructing the 5/5/8 full carbon ring system in natural product synthesis. In continuation with our ongoing studies towards the total synthesis of structurally complex natural products by using new strategy and method,<sup>[17]</sup> we were curious whether Yu’s [5+2+1] reaction could be applied for the preparation of such full carbon ring system. If successful, it could not only extend the application of [5+2+1] reaction, but also facilitate the efficient preparation of kalmane diterpenoids. Herein, we report a general and powerful approach for the efficient construction of the 5/5/8/5 tetracyclic skeleton of kalmane diterpenoids, and achieve the practical total synthesis of (+)-kalmanol (1).

Our retrosynthetic analysis is depicted in Scheme 1. We envisioned that (+)-kalmanol (2) could be generated from the tetracycle 3 through late-stage functional group transformations to install five hydroxyl groups (Scheme 1). The right cyclopentenone moiety of 3 could be constructed by a sequence of allylation, Wacker oxidation, and intramolecular aldol condensation reaction of tricycle 4. The 5/5/8 tricyclic ring system of 4 could be efficiently accessed by using the Rh-catalyzed [5+2+1] cycloaddition of 1-enevinylcyclopropane (VCP) precursor 5 and CO. In turn, the olefin 5 could be easily synthesized from the known Maimone’s enone (6),<sup>[18]</sup> which could be readily prepared in two steps from the commercially available (�)-linalool.

Our synthesis commenced with the preparation of tetracycle 3 (Scheme 2a). Cu-catalyzed 1,4-addition of the butenyl magnesium bromide to enone 6 in the presence of chlorotrimethylsilane (TMSCl) provided the corresponding silyl enol ether, which was filtrated and directly used to regenerate the enolate anion with methyllithium followed by O-triflation with Comins’ reagent to afford 7 in 82% yield.<sup>[9]</sup> The Iron-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions of cyclopropyl magnesium bromide and O-triflate 7 gave the desired ene-VCP 5 in 91 % yield.<sup>[19]</sup> With the ene-VCP 5 in hand, the Rh-catalyzed [5+2+1] cycloaddition reaction was immediately investigated (See Scheme 2b). It was found that the solvent and the reaction temperature were important to obtain higher yield. Under the optimized reaction conditions, the desired tricycle ketone 4 was obtained in 67% yield. The structure of 4 was determined by X-ray crystallography.<sup>[20]</sup> It should be mentioned that the Rhcatalyzed [5+2+1] reaction can be scaled up to 5 g scale.

With a robust route to 4 established, allylation of 4 with KHMDS, BEt and allyl iodide gave the ketone 8 as a single isomer in 92% yield.<sup>[21]</sup> Tsuji-Wacker oxidation of 8 gave the 1,4-diketone 9 in 89 % yield. Unexpectedly, aldol condensation cyclization of diketone 9 was also challenging. After numerous trials (See Scheme 2c and Supporting Information for details), we found that reaction with KOH in EtOH/THF gave the desired tetracycle 10 in 77 % yield, along with the C5-epi-9 in 11% yield which could be used to regenerate tetracycle 10 (dr =3: 1) under the same conditions above.<sup>[21]</sup> The epimerization at C5 occurred on diketone 9 rather than tetracycle 10. (Control experiments see SI). Methylation of 10 with NaH and MeI gave 3 in 92% yield $( 2 . 2 \ \mathrm { g }$ in one sequence from enone 6), thus achieving the construction of the intact 5/5/8/5 tetracyclic system of the kalmane diterpenoids.

raw_text: Protection of 1,3-diol at C16 and C8 of triol 13 with benzylidene acetal followed by elimination of C5-OH gave the diene 14 in 95% yield in a one-pot fashion. Regio- and stereo-selective dihydroxylation of C5�C6 alkene of 14 afforded the corresponding diol which was subsequently protected with methoxymethyl (MOM) group to furnish enone 15 in 85 % overall yield.<sup>[25]</sup> γ-Hydroxylation at C10 of enone 15 with $t – \mathrm { B u O K } / \mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$ followed by protection of the resulting C10-hydroxyl group with chlorotriethylsilane (TESCl) gave the enone 16 in 72 % yield in a one-pot fashion. It should be mentioned that the solvent of this reaction was pivotal and low yields were obtained when the tetrahydrofuran, N, N-dimethylformamide and toluene were used.

raw_text: Diisobutyl aluminium hydride (DIBAL�H) reduction of ketone 16 followed by MOM protection of the corresponding alcohol afforded olefin 17 in 95 % yield. Removal of triethylsilane (TES) in 17 with TBAF, Dess–Martin periodinane (DMP) oxidation of the resulting alcohol, followed by epimerization of C9 configuration with DBU gave the enone 18 in 81% overall yield. The driving force of epimerization of C9 configuration might be the release of transannular strain of $\mathrm { C } 7$ and C10 (ΔG=�2.46 kcal/mol, see Supporting Information for the energy calculations). Treatment of enone 18 with methyl cerium chloride gave alcohol 19 in 99 % yield.<sup>[26]</sup> And other methyl anion reagents (MeLi and MeMgBr) did not give the desired product. The high stereoselectivity of the reaction might be explained by the directed influence of MOM group. Reduction of 19 with $\mathrm { P d } ( \mathrm { O H } ) _ { 2 } / \mathrm { C }$ and $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } ,$ accompanied with the simultaneous removal of benzylidene acetal, gave triol 20 in 99 % yield. Finally, global removal of the MOM protecting groups of 20 with $\mathrm { R u O } _ { 4 }$ and KOH furnished (+)-kalmanol (1).<sup>[27]</sup> All analytical data (<sup>1</sup>H NMR, <sup>13</sup>C NMR, HRMS, and $[ a ] _ { \mathrm { D } } )$ of the synthesized 1 matched that reported for the natural product.<sup>[1]</sup> It is noteworthy that over 300 mg of (+)-kalmanol was prepared, demonstrating the scalability potential of our synthetic route.

raw_text: The significant analgesic effects and preliminary structure–activity relationship analysis of kalmanol had been investigated by Yao and Yu group.<sup>[2]</sup> However, its bioactivity on voltage-gated sodium channels has not been reported as far as we know. As an analogue of grayanotoxins, potent inhibitors of the voltage-gated sodium channel $\mathrm { N a } _ { \mathrm { V } } 1 . 4 , \AA ^ { [ 2 8 ] }$ kalmanol could also be a $\mathrm { N a } _ { \mathrm { V } } 1 . 4$ blocker. To verify this hypothesis, the inhibitory effect of kalmanol on $\mathrm { N a } _ { \mathrm { V } } 1 . 4$ was examined (Figure S1). Our biological evaluation revealed that kalmanol inhibited the human $\mathrm { N a } _ { \mathrm { V } } 1 . 4$ channels expressed in CHO cells with $\mathrm { I C } _ { 5 0 }$ values of $1 9 9 . 3 \mu \mathrm { M }$ and 19.6 μM for resting state and half-inactivated state, respectively (Figure S1b), which indicated kalmanol bound to the inactivated state of $\mathrm { N a } _ { \mathrm { V } } 1 . 4$ channels with high affinity but bound only weakly to channels in the resting state. In addition, the electrophysiological data showed that the voltage-dependent fast inactivation of $\mathrm { N a v } 1 . 4$ were dramatically shifted to hyperpolarized potential by roughly 17 mV in the presence of 20 μM kalmanol (Figure S1d). These results may suggest that kalmanol is a state-dependent inhibitor of $\mathrm { N a } _ { \mathrm { v } } 1$ .4 and inhibits the channel by stabilizing an inactivated state.

raw_text: In summary, we have accomplished the efficient total synthesis of (+)-kalmanol in 22 steps with 2.3% overall yield from the readily available enone 3. The central featured strategy in the synthesis was a powerful intramolecular Rh(I)-catalyzed [5+2+1] cycloaddition to construct the 5/5/8 skeleton. To our best knowledge, this is the first application of the Rh-catalyzed [5+2+1] cycloaddition reaction to construct the 5/5/8 full carbon ring system in natural product synthesis. In addition, a rare oxidation relay by C3 ketone was applied to construct the oxidation state of C5 and C10. Finally the preliminary biological activity suggested the inhibitory effects of the kalmanol on voltage-gated sodium channel $\mathrm { N a } _ { \mathrm { V } } 1 . 4$
